## META

A chat as two files in the project's `.inksprite/chats/`: its row as
`<id>.json`, and its messages as `<id>.jsonl`, one to a line, in the order
they were made.

A chat can run to tens of megabytes, and while a reply streams in it is
saved every half second, so the messages are not rewritten whole when
only the end of them changed: a new message is added at the end, and the
one being written over and over is written again where it starts. Only a
change further back, an edit or a summary put above earlier turns,
rewrites the file. The row changes on every turn, so it is a file of its
own and small.

## planMessages

How to write a chat's messages, from what its file holds and what changed.

- `append` - Write `text` from byte `at` on, and end the file there: the
  lines before `at` stay as they are. For new messages at the end, and
  the last one written again.
- `rewrite` - Anything further back: the file is to be read, changed and
  written whole (`mergeMessages`).

A read passes over a line it cannot read, so a stop partway through an
append leaves the lines before it, and a whole write is made whole or not
at all.

### Parameters

- `previous` **([MessageLines][19] | null)** What the file holds; null when there is no file
- `puts` **[Array][393]\<Message>** Messages new or changed
- `deleted` **Iterable<[string][392]>** Messages gone

Returns **({op: `"append"`, at: [number][395], text: [string][392], lines: [MessageLines][19]} | {op: `"rewrite"`} | null)** Null when nothing changed

## withFrontmatter

A document as a file, and back.

A text document is a markdown file, its row in frontmatter and its content
as the body. A folder's row is its `.folder.md`, the summary as the body.
An imported file is itself, with a hidden markdown file beside it carrying
its row and the text read out of it. A repository keeps its own row and
the rows of everything in it in one `.repository.json` inside it; its files
are their text.

The frontmatter is the row, less what the file already says (the body,
where the file is, what kind of file it is) and what is worked out (the
word count, the version). Whatever else a row holds goes in as it is, so a
field added to documents later reaches the disk without anything here
changing. Times are written as dates and read back as milliseconds.

## withFrontmatter

A file of these fields and this body. One blank line comes between them,
and nothing after the body: what is read back is what was written.

### Parameters

- `fields` **Record<[string][392], [unknown][206]>**&#x20;
- `body` **[string][392]**&#x20;

Returns **[string][392]**&#x20;

## storage

Where the app's rows are kept.

The one module that reads and writes the database; nothing else imports
`stores/db.js`, and lint says so. The stores hold rows in memory and hand
their changes to `syncStore`, which writes them here; everything they read
that is not already in memory comes from here too.

The rows fall in two kinds:

- **Project tables** - `stories`, `documents`, `files`, `chats` and
  `messages`: a project and everything in it. They are read the ways the
  app reads them (a project's tree, a chat's messages, a file's bytes)
  rather than as tables, because in the desktop app they are to live in a
  folder of files, where those reads are cheap and a query across every
  project is not.
- **App tables** - the writer's connections, presets, prompts, profiles,
  skills and MCP servers, and the jobs under way: configuration and work
  on this copy of the app, which stays in IndexedDB everywhere. They are
  read and written as plain tables.

On the web all of it is Dexie (`dexie.js`). In the desktop app the
projects are in a folder the writer chose, and the rest is Dexie still
(`library.js`, chosen as the app opens by `open.js`). What a project is as a folder
of files, for the desktop app, is here too, as plain functions over rows
and paths that touch no disk:

- **layout** - Where each document of a project goes, and the documents a
  folder holds when it is read back
- **documents** - One document as its file: frontmatter and body, or the
  hidden file beside an imported one, or a repository's list
- **names** - Filenames made from titles that every system takes
- **frontmatter** - YAML at the top of a markdown file
- **plan** - The moves, trashes and writes from one layout to the next
- **chats** - A chat's row and messages, written only where they changed
- **library** - Storage in the library, through the main process's files
- **open** - Which storage the app opens with, and the window's projects
  moved into the library the first time

Design: `.llm/markdown_library_design.md`, step 3.

### Examples

```javascript
import { storage } from '@/storage/index.js'

const documents = await storage.documents(storyId)
const presets = await storage.all('aiProfiles')
```

## filenameFor

A project as a folder: where each document goes, and the documents a
folder holds.

    My Novel/
      .folder.md                the root: id, title, summary
      .inksprite/
        story.json              the project's own row, and the schema it is in
        narration/<id>.json     who speaks which block of a document
        chats/                  see chats.js
        moving/                 where a move puts something out of the way
      Manuscript/               an ordered folder
        .folder.md
        01 - Act 1/
          01 - Chapter 1.md
      Notes/
        Elara.md
        Rulebook.pdf            an imported file, as it was imported
        .Rulebook.pdf.md        its row and the text read out of it
        tool/                   a repository: its files as they are
          .repository.json      every row in it, by path
          src/main.js

A file is named from its title (names.js), with its place first in an
ordered folder. A name in use is taken by the first in the order the
folder shows, and the rest get `(2)` and on. Nothing internal names a
path: ids are in the files, so a document keeps its id however it moves.

## STORY_FILE

The project's row.

## MOVING

Where a move puts what stands in its way, until it can go where it goes.

## readProject

The documents a project's folder holds.

Its files are taken as they are, edits made elsewhere and all. A file
renamed somewhere else is that title now. In an ordered folder the order
is the order of the prefixes, numbered again from the top; in any other,
the order of the titles. A file with no id, or frontmatter that cannot be
read, is a document under a new id. A folder with no `.folder.md`, or a
file that is neither markdown nor beside a row, is not read, and is left
as it is. What a move had put out of the way when the app stopped comes
back at the top of the project.

## nanoid

Storage in the library: the desktop app's projects as folders of files in
the folder the writer chose, and the app's own tables in IndexedDB, as on
the web.

The disk is the main process's (`electron/src/library.js`), reached through
`disk`: paths below the library, and the few things that can be done there.
What a project is as files is `layout.js`, and what a change of rows does to
them `plan.js`; this keeps where each project is, what it last saw of each
file, and turns the stores' changes into plans.

Only a sketch of each project is kept here, its rows without their text:
the stores hold the text, and what is asked for is read from the disk
again. Everything is done one call at a time, in the order asked.

## load

Read a project's folder whole and hand back its documents with their
text. The first time, the sketch of it is kept: a document found without
an id has its file written again with one, and a project written at an
older schema is brought forward and written again. After that the sketch
is what the stores' own writes made it, and a read leaves it alone: a
read numbers each folder's documents from the top, where the stores may
have numbered them otherwise, and the two mixed would put a folder on
disk in an order the app does not show.

### Parameters

- `project` **[Project][221]**&#x20;

Returns **[Promise][401]<[Array][393]<[Document][398]>>**&#x20;

## UNSAFE

Filenames made from titles.

A title is the writer's and can hold anything; a filename has to be one
that macOS, Windows and Linux all take, and that a case-insensitive disk
keeps apart from its neighbours. Names in a folder are compared the way
those disks compare them: composed the same way and in any case.

## UNSAFE

What no system takes in a name, or Windows does not: control characters among them.

## RESERVED

Names Windows keeps for devices, whatever comes after a dot.

## MAX_BYTES

The most a name made from a title takes, in UTF-8 bytes. Disks allow 255;
this leaves room for an order prefix, a `(2)`, and a hidden file's `.` and
`.md` beside an imported file.

Type: [number][395]

## PREFIX

An order prefix: `07 - `.

## clip

A name cut to fit, on a character's edge.

- `name` **[string][392]**&#x20;

Returns **[string][392]**&#x20;

## safeName

A title as a name every system takes: the characters none of them allow
as hyphens, no leading dot (which would hide it), none of the endings
Windows drops, nothing Windows keeps for a device, and not too long.

### Parameters

- `title` **[string][392]**&#x20;

Returns **[string][392]**&#x20;

## nameKey

What to do to a project's folder: the files a project is, and the moves,
trashes and writes that take its folder from one layout to the next.

A change of rows is a change of layout (layout.js), and the difference
between the two is the plan. A document whose path changed is moved,
folders whole, so a renamed folder is one rename however much is in it.
One that is gone goes to the trash, a folder whole unless something kept
is still in it. One that is new or changed is written. Nothing is written
that did not change, and nothing is ever deleted outright.

A move whose way is blocked, by something itself still to move (two
documents trading names) or by something on its way out, first moves what
is there out of the way, into `.inksprite/moving/`, and on from there.

## splitExtension

A name split at its extension, where it has one: `Map.png` is `Map` and
`.png`. A leading dot is not an extension.

### Parameters

- `name` **[string][392]**&#x20;

Returns **{stem: [string][392], extension: [string][392]}**&#x20;

## isDesktop

Which storage the app opens with: IndexedDB in a browser, and in the
desktop app, when the writer keeps the projects in a folder, the library
in the app's data folder, the app's own tables in IndexedDB still.

The first time the desktop app opens on a library, the projects it kept
in the window until then are written into it, each as a project of its
own. The window's copy is left as it was. Keeping them in the app again
copies the library's back over it first, so nothing done since is lost.

as it is now, takes the place of the app's own, and the library is let go
of. Its files stay where they are. The app is to open again after; until
then the library is still the storage, and a copy that fails leaves it so.

### Parameters

- `library` **[Storage][116]** The storage open on the library

##

Type: any

## Op

One thing to do to the folder. Paths are below the project folder.

- `move` - A file or a folder, with all that is in it, to where nothing is
- `trash` - A file or a folder to the system's trash
- `write` - A file's whole text, made whole or not at all

Type: ({op: `"move"`, from: [string][392], to: [string][392]} | {op: `"trash"`, path: [string][392]} | {op: `"write"`, path: [string][392], text: [string][392]})

## depthOf

### Parameters

- `path` **[string][392]**&#x20;

## isBelow

### Parameters

- `path` **[string][392]** @param {string} dir
- `dir` &#x20;

## isFolder

### Parameters

- `kind` **[EntryKind][149]**&#x20;

## filesOf

The files an entry is, less a repository's own file, which is made from
all that is in it (`repositoryText`), and an imported file's bytes, which
are written when they come.

### Parameters

- `entry` **[Entry][150]**&#x20;
- `document` **[Document][398]**&#x20;

Returns **[Array][393]<{path: [string][392], text: [string][392]}>**&#x20;

## repositoryText

A repository's `.repository.json`, from where everything in it is.

### Parameters

- `repository` **[Entry][150]**&#x20;
- `entries` **[Map][397]<[string][392], [Entry][150]>**&#x20;
- `documentOf` &#x20;

Returns **{path: [string][392], text: [string][392]}**&#x20;

## below

Type: [Array][393]<{path: [string][392], document: [Document][398]}>

## documentOf

Type: [Document][398]

## narrationText

A narration file's text.

### Parameters

- `document` **[Document][398]**&#x20;

## projectFiles

Every file of a project but its chats and the bytes of its imported files:
what writing it into an empty folder writes.

### Parameters

- `story` **Story**&#x20;
- `schema` **[number][395]** The schema version its rows are in
- `entries` **[Map][397]<[string][392], [Entry][150]>** Its layout
- `documentOf` &#x20;

Returns **[Map][397]<[string][392], [string][392]>** Text by path below the project folder

## storyText

The project's own file: its row, and the schema the rows are in.

### Parameters

- `story` **Story**&#x20;
- `schema` **[number][395]**&#x20;

Returns **[string][392]**&#x20;
